title: Edge chunk coalescence causes tool-call boundary loss and structured output parser failures
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent failures when invoking tool/function calls that return mixed content (JSON metadata interleaved with binary attachments or base64 blobs). Failures manifest as: parser exceptions, truncated JSON fields, or tool outputs being merged across adjacent requests. The error surface is most common when requests traverse our regional edge proxy with TLS termination + gzip-enabled responses and when small successive chunks are coalesced by the proxy or edge TCP stack.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure a tool invocation that emits alternating JSON chunks and binary/base64 attachment segments with explicit chunk separators
2) Send high-frequency calls from a client through the regional edge (example: eu-west1) with keep-alive enabled
3) Observe responses on the client and runtime side; the proxy may coalesce small TCP frames and reorder headers when gzip is enabled
4) Reproduce more reliably with simulated network conditions: 30ms RTT, packet coalescing enabled, and concurrent streams > 50
technical_root_cause: When edge TLS termination + gzip content-encoding is enabled, the regional proxy sometimes coalesces adjacent response chunks and drops our implicit per-chunk boundary markers. For payloads containing non-UTF8 bytes (attachments) the coalesced buffer can shift delimiter positions. Downstream structured-output parser assumed preserved chunk framing and performed strict UTF-8 decodes, leading to field truncation and JSON parse errors. In Dedicated and Private setups an additional proxy layer (customer-managed ingress) introduced variations in chunk sizes and ordering, exposing the same bug under different timing conditions.
investigation_notes: Observed correlation between gzip-enabled responses and incidence rate — disabling gzip at the edge materially reduced failures in a canary customer (incidence 0/48h)
tcpdump at runtime host shows merged frames where our boundary bytes (0x1E 0x0A) moved to the middle of base64 segment
Parser stacktrace points to strict decoder failing on first non-utf8 byte rather than skipping to next JSON object
Reproduced locally by forcing proxy to join writev fragments; adding a header-preservation patch to the proxy mitigates the issue
fix_summary: Short-term: ship a defensive parser change that tolerates interleaved non-UTF8 segments and searches for the next valid JSON boundary rather than failing hard. Also add an explicit per-chunk ASCII boundary marker in outgoing tool-call responses (unambiguous token) to make boundaries resilient to coalescence. Medium-term: update edge proxy write logic to respect original chunk boundaries (preserve writev segmentation) and add option to disable content coalescing for tool-call endpoints. Long-term: add integration tests that exercise gzip + TLS termination + chunk coalescing scenarios.
implementation_changes: 1) runtime/parser: make JSON extractor resilient by scanning for ASCII boundary token and skipping non-UTF8 prefix bytes

2) runtime/protocol: include explicit boundary header 'X-Redwood-Chunk-Boundary' and emit '--rdw-boundary
' before each chunk payload
3) edge/proxy: add config flag 'preserve_chunk_segment' default false and a bugfix to avoid combining adjacent writev segments for tool endpoints
4) add e2e test harness that runs with gzip enabled, simulates coalescing, and validates parser output
rollout_plan: A) Ship defensive parser and explicit boundary marker to canary namespace (hosted) - runtime-1.22-canary - 2026-03-08
B) Monitor canary for 72 hours, track 'toolcall_parse_error_rate' and 'customer_reported_failures' dashboards
C) If stable, rollout to hosted production over 48 hours with weighted traffic shift (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
D) For Dedicated customers, coordinate with account owners to schedule a hotfix window and provide an opt-in proxy flag; provide patch for on-prem proxy with instructions
E) For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, provide hotfix bundle and manual upgrade instructions and offer remote assist for customers with custom ingress
qa_checks: Unit tests for parser tolerant behavior including mixed non-UTF8 prefixes
Integration tests simulating proxy coalescing + gzip enabled
Load test with 500 concurrent tool invocations to ensure no perf regression
Canary validation: zero parity loss and parse error rate < 0.01% over 72h
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: >3% increase in toolcall_parse_error_rate in 10m window triggers P0
Dashboard: per-region incidence, gzip_enabled vs disabled comparison, customer-scoped timelines
Synthetic check: daily cross-region run that invokes mixed-chunk tool and verifies structured output correctness
risk_and_tradeoffs: Defensive parser increases CPU per request slightly (measured ~3% in canary) — acceptable for P0 customer impact
Adding explicit ASCII boundary increases payload size marginally but makes parsing robust across proxies
Proxy change to preserve writev segments is safest but may require deeper testing across vendor proxies and could be disruptive to existing edge optimizations
For Dedicated/Private deployments we need customer coordination to avoid unexpected behavior during proxy upgrade
postmortem_actions: Create runbook section for tool-call structured parsing incidents
Add integration scenarios to CI for content-encoding + proxy behavior
Engage solutions engineering to outreach to affected customers and provide incident timelines and recommended mitigations
Consider making 'boundary-preservation' default in runtime after 1 release of observation
